name: chicken pot pie
instructions:
Poached-and-shredded chicken breast in a leek-carrot-celery rosemary gravy, filled into a pie with a real pastry top.

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. POACH THE CHICKEN: poach shreddable chicken breast in chicken broth with a BAY LEAF. Chip it up, put it in knee-deep in braising liquid, and instapot at LOW PRESSURE for 5 MINUTES. Low pressure is preferred because it gets cooking faster and the chicken doesn't sit in boiling water as long. Keep the poaching stock — it becomes the gravy liquid.
2. SAUTÉ THE VEGETABLES: in a big frying pan, sauté leeks + carrots + celery + garlic + rosemary in a MIX OF BUTTER AND OLIVE OIL. (Thyme works as well, but chicken pot pie has a strong preference for rosemary — see notes.)
3. FLOUR WHEN THE LIQUID GOES AWAY: add flour once the pan liquid has cooked off. Stir well so all the vegetables are covered and NO WHITE FLOUR is visible.
4. LIQUID IN: pour in the chicken stock you poached the breast in, plus more to fill the pot. Add a bit of cream.
5. STEW COVERED until the carrots are cooked, then UNCOVER until it becomes a thick gravy.
6. BEURRE MANIE to thicken further, until desired.
7. PEAS AND POTATOES TOWARD THE END: both work well, but add them late. Peas are low risk; potatoes can get overcooked or undercooked easily — FINELY DICE them so they're predictable.
8. CHICKEN IN AT THE END: shred and add the poached breast last, then fill the pie.
9. TOP AND BAKE: a REAL PIE TOP is ideal for this recipe ([[savory-pie-crust]]). Gratining with breadcrumbs + spray oil is a good option too — use DEVILED BREADCRUMBS, superior to regular breadcrumbs here (see notes).
notes:
=== ROSEMARY IS THE HERB ===

Thyme works as well, but chicken pot pie has a strong preference for ROSEMARY. JULIA CHILD OPTS FOR TARRAGON AND PARSLEY — I skip both.

=== LOW-PRESSURE POACH — WHY ===

Instapot LOW pressure, 5 minutes, chicken knee-deep in broth with a bay leaf. Low pressure is preferred because it gets cooking faster and the chicken doesn't sit in boiling water as long — gentler on the breast, which needs to stay shreddable, not rubbery. The poaching liquid double-dips as the gravy stock.

=== REAL CHICKEN STOCK OVER BOUILLON ===

Real chicken stock (the perishable kind) is better than bouillon here. Bouillon is probably fine — it's a gravy, so it can handle a little MSG — but chicken pot pie is kind of an ordeal to make, so I don't like to risk it.

=== THE GRAVY BUILD — FLOUR ON THE VEGETABLES, THEN STOCK, THEN REDUCE ===

The flour goes on the sautéed vegetables once their liquid has cooked off — stirred until no white flour is visible — before any stock goes in (roux-on-the-vegetables, not a separate roux). Then the poaching stock + more stock + a bit of cream, covered until the carrots are done, uncovered to reduce to a thick gravy, and a beurre manie to close the gap to the thickness you want.

=== PEAS BELONG HERE ===

Peas work well in a pot pie specifically because all the resulting gravy is consumed inside the pie — no broth is left behind on the plate, no bowl-bottom puddle. Peas are small enough to be eaten alongside the other components in every bite, they add an earthy vegetal note that the cream-rosemary-chicken base doesn't otherwise carry, and they bring more protein. They're not a standard chicken-stew addition (in a fricassee they'd get lost in a deep bowl of sauce), but the pot-pie format makes them earn their place. Add toward the end — low risk.

=== POTATOES FOR STARCH WITHOUT MSG GUMMINESS — FINELY DICED, ADDED LATE ===

Potatoes add starchy body that thickens the final filling and gives it more chew. This matters because the alternative — pushing the gravy thicker with more bouillon/MSG or more flour — leaves the filling gummy and one-note. Potatoes do the thickening structurally instead of chemically; the dish reads richer without reading artificial. They're the risky late addition though: easy to overcook or undercook — FINELY DICE them so they're predictable.

=== DIJON — SECONDARY, ONLY WITH A POTATO ELEMENT ===

Dijon mustard is secondary — but I wouldn't include it unless you opted for a potato element.

=== FINELY CHOPPED, NOT PROCESSED — BITE-SIZED FOR THE GRAVY ===

Every component (leeks, celery, carrots, potatoes, chicken) should be finely chopped but kept bite-sized — not pulverized in a food processor. The goal is a cohesive gravy solution where each forkful has a bit of everything in it. Knife-and-cutting-board instincts are right here. Processor-fine vegetables dissolve into the cream base and lose textural identity; large rustic-chunk cuts leave you fishing for specific components rather than eating a unified bite. Aim for the size that survives the bake but disappears against the others on the fork.

=== TOP — REAL PIE CRUST FIRST; DEVILED BREADCRUMBS THE GRATIN PICK ===

A real pastry pie top ([[savory-pie-crust]]) is ideal for this recipe. The breadcrumb + spray-oil gratin is a good option too — and DEVILED BREADCRUMBS are the pick there, superior to regular breadcrumbs.
